name: Anti-imperialism
summary: Anti-imperialism opposes colonial rule, foreign domination and great-power intervention, and upholds the right of peoples to govern themselves. Its mainstream, in the Leninist and Third World tradition, ties imperialism to capitalist monopoly and finance capital, and holds that formal independence means little while economies stay dependent on the former rulers.
scope: The mainstream 20th-century anti-colonial and Third World strand: Lenin's Imperialism, Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth, and the Bandung-era non-aligned movement. It leans left and secular. It does not cover the Islamist and right-wing anti-imperialisms described in the Wikipedia overview, which would answer religion, state and economy questions differently, nor Hobson's liberal strand in full.

keyFigures.name: Vladimir Lenin
keyFigures.role: Author of Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism, the founding Marxist theory of imperialism.

keyFigures.name: Frantz Fanon
keyFigures.role: Theorist of decolonization and neocolonialism, author of The Wretched of the Earth.

keyFigures.name: J. A. Hobson
keyFigures.role: Author of Imperialism: A Study (1902), the liberal critique that influenced Lenin.

sources.title: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism, ch. 7
sources.author: V. I. Lenin (1916)
sources.usedFor: Imperialism as monopoly and finance capital, war from redivision of the world, rejection of ultra-imperialism.

sources.title: The Pitfalls of National Consciousness (The Wretched of the Earth, ch. 3)
sources.author: Frantz Fanon (1961)
sources.usedFor: Neocolonial dependence, the native middle class, one-party rule, tribalism, nationalization through cooperatives.

sources.title: Anti-imperialism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Strands of the ideology and positions on self-determination, capitalism, intervention and internationalism.

sources.title: Bandung Conference
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Condemnation of colonialism, non-intervention, UN Charter, human rights, limits on big-power defence pacts, economic cooperation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern as such; inferred from the left-leaning anti-colonial mainstream, which expected independent states to provide social services.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream; wage policy is not part of the anti-imperialist core.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Fanon sees the post-colonial market economy as a channel for foreign capital and a parasitic native middle class; inferred, since strands differ.

public-ownership.rationale: Fanon proposes nationalizing trade through cooperatives, and post-colonial states commonly nationalized foreign-held industries to break dependence.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Hobson's liberal strand proposed taxing surplus wealth to remove the drive to empire; the broader anti-colonial left leans the same way.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the left-wing majority; the unions were allies of many anti-colonial movements but this is not a defining position.

property-fundamental.rationale: Lenin and Fanon treat property in the hands of monopolies and foreign firms as an instrument of domination; inferred, not a central claim.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-imperialists target multinational and monopoly firms as agents of economic domination and favor curbing them.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream; not directly addressed.

worker-ownership.rationale: Marxist strands favor it and Fanon backs cooperatives, but liberal and nationalist strands are indifferent, so adherents are split.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anti-imperialists typically see counter-terror surveillance as a tool of Western power; inferred and uneven across strands.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The ideology is indifferent; adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; strands split between liberal and nationalist or Marxist views.

strong-leader.rationale: Fanon warns that the nationalist leader shields elite corruption and turns the party into a tool of control, though many independence leaders were strong figures.

state-harmful.rationale: Anti-colonial movements seek sovereign states of their own, and Fanon criticises specific states rather than the state itself.

empower-police-military.rationale: Anti-imperialists generally oppose military buildup by great powers; for post-colonial states they favor self-defence, so inferred and mixed.

decide-locally.rationale: Fanon calls for decentralized, mass-rooted political organization, but anti-colonial states also stress national unity; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from left-leaning mainstream; not addressed.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed; secular-Marxist and traditionalist strands diverge.

more-religion-public.rationale: Secular nationalist and Marxist strands dominate; Islamist anti-imperialists would disagree, so this is a weak lean.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Condemnation of racial domination and colonial legacies is part of the anti-colonial tradition (Bandung condemned colonialism in all its manifestations).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Anti-colonial movements defend national culture against colonial erasure, a theme Fanon develops, though he also criticises its romanticization.

gradual-change.rationale: Anti-colonial movements demanded rapid independence and rejected gradual reform within empire; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anti-imperialists tend to see powerful international bodies as dominated by the great powers and stress state sovereignty, though they defend the UN Charter.

free-trade.rationale: Lenin holds that finance capital deepens inequality between countries, and post-colonial thought sees free trade as perpetuating dependence.

nation-first.rationale: Anti-imperialists oppose great-power self-interest, yet back each nation's own sovereignty; for a great power's citizen the stance is to reject national-interest primacy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Non-intervention in internal affairs was a Bandung principle, and humanitarian grounds are viewed as pretexts for imperial intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between internationalist and sovereignty-minded views.

limit-growth.rationale: Post-colonial thought prioritizes development of poor countries; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; strands split on who bears the burden, though many demand rich-country responsibility.

revolution-justified.rationale: Armed and revolutionary struggle against colonial rule is central, from Lenin's support of national uprisings to Fanon on the Algerian war.

experts-over-public.rationale: Fanon distrusts the educated elite cut off from the masses and urges mass political education; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands favor planning and Fanon speaks of popular planning, but liberal and nationalist strands do not.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fiscal design is outside anti-imperialist concerns; no strand or text takes a side on this tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Hobson's liberal strand backs taxes on unearned wealth; inferred for the rest.

basic-income.rationale: Anti-imperialist writings never address unconditional income transfers, and strands would split along left-right lines.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Post-colonial states sought to build domestic industry and reduce dependence on former colonial powers, which Fanon contrasts with a middleman economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Bandung called for reducing economic dependence on industrial powers, and post-colonial development states directed investment accordingly.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Fanon backs cooperatives and Marxists collective ownership, while nationalists accept peasant smallholding, so no common view emerges.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only the Marxist-Leninist strand holds this, and only as a distant goal.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; inferred, since the free-market premise opposes the left-leaning mainstream.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-run bargaining bodies are a fascist-era idea that the anti-colonial sources do not take up, and strands differ on it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Fanon calls the one-party state the bourgeoisie's dictatorship in open form, yet Leninist and many post-colonial states used it, so adherents are split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anti-colonial movements largely favored republics; some accommodated monarchies, so a weak lean.

democracy-best.rationale: Self-government is the aim, but Leninist strand is skeptical of liberal democracy; inferred.

direct-votes.rationale: Fanon favors mass participation; no stated position on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Marxist strands favor it; liberal and nationalist strands do not.

right-to-secede.rationale: Lenin defends the right of nations to separate as part of self-determination, and anti-colonial movements claimed it against empires.

natural-rulers.rationale: Imperial rule was justified by claims that some peoples are fit to rule others; anti-imperialism rejects that premise.

political-violence-never.rationale: Fanon and Lenin treat anti-colonial violence as legitimate, and the mainstream doesn't renounce armed struggle against occupation.

war-builds-character.rationale: Lenin condemns imperialist war as a product of capitalist rivalry, but Fanon, also in scope, describes anti-colonial violence as cleansing and unifying for the colonised people; the tradition does not give one answer.

separate-church-state.rationale: Secular nationalists and Marxists say yes, Islamist anti-imperialists say no.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Only the Islamist strand holds this; the mainstream here is secular.

military-superiority.rationale: Anti-imperialism opposes great-power military dominance and arms races as tools of empire.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Fanon warns that tribal and ethnic loyalty replaces genuine national consciousness, though nationalist strands vary.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist-Leninist strands hold it and see imperialism as class rule on a world scale; liberal and nationalist strands don't, giving a weaker lean.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Opposition to settler colonialism and dispossession leads most adherents to support indigenous land claims.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Post-colonial thought widely holds that colonial powers owe redress for exploitation, though the Wikipedia overview does not give a unified doctrine.

civilizational-union.rationale: Islamist and pan-regional strands favor it; secular nationalists favor state sovereignty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is not a topic of the core texts, and adherents hold varied views on it.

limit-population.rationale: Post-colonial thinkers often see population control campaigns as imperial; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anti-colonial development thinking aims at industrialization; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Anti-imperialists want technology transfer to poor countries but have no shared view on speeding up disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is not discussed in the anti-colonial tradition, and adherents hold no common view.

algorithmic-government.rationale: AI governance is anachronistic for the core texts, and adherents are split between skeptics of Western tech power and modernizers.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The ideology has no stated view on encryption, though opposition to state surveillance would pull some adherents toward yes.

restore-past-order.rationale: Anti-colonial movements look forward to a new society, though some invoke precolonial heritage; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred from the committed, ideologically driven character of the movement.

direct-action.rationale: Fanon sees mass struggle as forming consciousness, and independence movements used strikes, boycotts and armed struggle alongside elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Fanon connects forms of struggle to the society that results, but Leninists accept any means, so adherents are split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not a position of any strand; inferred from the development aim.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Only marxist strands mention it, as a distant goal.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Marxist strands accept it as an eventual aim; other strands are indifferent.

production-for-use.rationale: Marxist strands favor it; liberal and nationalist strands do not.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Leninist account has capital export yielding profits from colonial labor; the liberal strand does not blame capitalism, so this is weaker than for Marxism proper.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Only Leninist strands hold it, the rest reject or ignore it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Lenin argues that redividing a fully divided world among monopoly capitalist powers can only be settled by war; Hobson's liberal strand dissents.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not a position of any strand; opposes the left-leaning mainstream.

harm-principle.rationale: This liberal rule about limiting state coercion is not addressed in anti-imperialist sources, and strands differ on it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Self-determination is a collective right of peoples, so anti-imperialism affirms group rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on collective self-government.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream and from the demand for economic as well as political independence.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; some strands hold that Western media serves empire, but the claim is about elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial hierarchy underpinned colonial ideology, and anti-colonial thought rejects it.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is a corporatist idea that anti-imperialist sources do not take up.

total-state.rationale: Fanon warns against a state that controls the masses, though Leninist strands accept strong states.

national-rebirth.rationale: Anti-colonial movements spoke of national awakening, but not in the sense of decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Opposition to expansion and domination abroad is the defining position.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not a position of any strand; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Forced labor was a feature of colonial rule that anti-colonial movements opposed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Postcolonial thinkers lean yes, while Leninist and liberal strands don't, so adherents are split.

universal-morality.rationale: Postcolonial thinkers question Western universalism, while liberal strands accept it; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Anti-imperialism does not address the philosophy of the common good, and Marxist, liberal and nationalist strands answer differently.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Many anti-imperialists view Zionism as settler colonialism and oppose it, but views vary, so a weak lean.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No anti-imperialist text covers diaspora citizenship; adherents split between the Palestinian right of return and the opposite view for other cases.

revive-national-language.rationale: Reviving or promoting indigenous languages is part of reclaiming national culture from colonial languages.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Marxist strands and Fanon's cooperatives lean yes, but liberal and nationalist strands are indifferent, so adherents are split.

rule-by-example.rationale: The ideology never addresses rule by moral example, apart from Fanon's call for mass political education over elite command.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-determination of nations is the defining claim of the ideology, and Lenin made it a programmatic demand.

force-without-un.rationale: Bandung's principles of non-intervention and adherence to the UN Charter bar unilateral use of force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular strands say yes; Islamist ones no.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anti-imperialism has no stated position on welfare eligibility for immigrants, and adherents are split between internationalist and national views.

class-collaboration.rationale: Lenin's account of a labour aristocracy bribed from colonial profits opposes class collaboration, though nationalist strands favor cross-class national fronts.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Fanon and anti-colonial movements defend cultural heritage against colonial destruction.

dominated-front.rationale: Bandung brought Afro-Asian states together against colonialism, and Third World solidarity is typical of the ideology.

workers-nation.rationale: Leninists favor international class solidarity while nationalist strands organize nationally.

ban-interest.rationale: Islamist strand supports it; others don't.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racial classification and segregation were instruments of colonial rule, and anti-imperialism rejects them.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist strand treats the state as the instrument of finance capital and ruling classes, though liberals dissent.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Producer-state and consumer-state adherents disagree, since many post-colonial economies depend on resource exports.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Anti-imperialism opposes forced assimilation of colonized peoples; weak inference for immigrants.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the core texts, and adherents hold varied views.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading one's government to other peoples is the imperial civilizing mission that anti-imperialism opposes.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Fanon depicts the post-colonial elite as an intermediary class shielding corruption, a recurring anti-colonial theme.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy was part of imperial racial ideology; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial demands for accountability for colonial violence.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Bandung's principles call for respect for fundamental human rights and equality of all races and nations.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Strand-dependent: Leninists divided over this, and non-Marxist strands don't address it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism is treated as a form of colonialism by anti-imperialists. The sources set out the underlying principle but do not state a position on this specific statement.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Colonial powers often ruled through separate religious laws, but anti-imperialist sources take no stated position on a uniform code.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The question of conversion is not covered by the core texts; secular strands lean against restrictions and religious strands the opposite.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: This is a regional religious question outside anti-imperialist doctrine, and adherents are split.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Leninist doctrine; other strands do not address it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Anti-colonial legitimacy rests on rule by the governed, not imposed from abroad, which echoes Bandung's stress on self-government.

trade-surplus.rationale: The aim of export surpluses is mercantilist; anti-imperialists focus on dependence, and no strand states a view on surplus targets.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of populations was a characteristic of colonial rule and settlement, and anti-imperialists oppose it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Anti-imperialists reject initiating force by great powers but endorse revolutionary violence against occupation, so the absolute principle is not held.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The social-Darwinist justification of empire is rejected by anti-imperialism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The question depends on who is deemed extremist, and anti-imperialist sources take no stated position.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Domination without active intervention, as in dependency, is what anti-imperialists object to, though no source states the republican formula.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional design is not a topic in the core texts, and Leninist and liberal strands differ on it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist strand yes; liberal and nationalist strands no.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream and concern for the poor countries.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy that anti-imperialist sources never address.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Anti-imperialists attribute poverty to exploitation by foreign capital, not to population growth.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Fanon sees ethnic division as a failure of national consciousness, but not as inherent to diversity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in anti-imperialist sources, and adherents have no shared view.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred; states of emergency were instruments of colonial rule.

party-controls-media.rationale: Leninist states did; Fanon and liberal strands would not.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Immigration rules are not covered by the core texts, and strands are split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Marxist strands favor it, others don't.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Leninist strands hold it; others don't.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Bandung stresses sovereignty and non-intervention, but regional unions among post-colonial states are favored by some, so a weak lean.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive design is not addressed, and post-colonial states chose both presidential and parliamentary systems.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance falls outside the ideology and no strand takes up the question.

clerical-rule.rationale: Only the Islamist strand supports it; the mainstream is secular.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin calls for revolutionary defeatism in imperialist wars among great powers, but liberal and nationalist strands don't, so adherents are split.

recall-officials.rationale: The recall of officials is not discussed in the core texts, though Fanon's mass participation could fit it, and adherents are split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Bandung says collective defence pacts should not serve big-power interests, and anti-imperialists oppose foreign bases and alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: Guerrilla warfare supports it in places, but it is not an ideological claim.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; Maoist strand leans yes.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunifying nations divided by colonial borders is a common anti-colonial aim, as in Vietnam and Korea.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Fanon criticizes the native educated bourgeoisie as detached from the masses, but not all university-educated people.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Bandung stressed equality of all nations and races, and anti-colonial thought rejects the claim that imperial civilization is higher.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not a shared position; Western-aligned regimes aside, adherents split between abolition and its use against terrorism or collaborators.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Education on sex and gender is outside the ideology, and secular and religious strands answer differently.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The topic is not covered in anti-imperialist sources, and secular and religious strands answer differently.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed in the core texts, and adherents hold varied views.

minority-language-support.rationale: Opposition to colonial language imposition extends to supporting suppressed languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general laws are not addressed by the core texts, and secular and religious strands answer differently.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Fanon notes that post-colonial budgets rest on foreign loans and gifts, and debt as dependence is a standard anti-imperialist complaint.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Fanon argues that political independence leaves the economy tied to the former colonizer, and Lenin ties imperialism to finance capital.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Post-colonial developmental states did this; Fanon criticizes the one-party state, so split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Aid is often seen as a means of dependence; reparations are favored, but not charity, so adherents are split.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing a head of state is not addressed by the core texts.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred; post-colonial thought sees monetary dependence as a tool of control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial settlements are not covered by general doctrine; adherents split between those who insist on historic homelands and those who favor compromise.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Maoist strand called the USSR social-imperialist, Leninists defend it; split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which sees environmental harm as an extractive cost imposed on the periphery; the principle is not an anti-imperialist concern as such.

collective-defense.rationale: Bandung limited collective defence arrangements that serve the interests of big powers, and non-aligned anti-imperialism opposes blocs such as NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Anti-imperialism rests on the self-determination of peoples and rejects conquest, so annexation against the people's will is unlawful occupation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The secular-left mainstream often curbs clerical power, but anti-colonial movements also drew on religion and the question is not core, so adherents are split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; anti-colonial states adopted both ceremonial presidencies and powerful partisan ones, and Fanon criticised one-party personal rule.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents are split: self-determination is central, yet Bandung-era states stressed territorial integrity against foreign meddling in separatist causes.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No settled view; adherents split between support for regional autonomy and suspicion that autonomy is a tool of foreign or colonial influence.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Anti-colonial movements of the left and secular mainstream stood for popular sovereignty and rejected divine-right monarchy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which expects redistributive, progressive taxation; tax structure is not part of the anti-imperialist core.

character-from-environment.rationale: Fanon and Lenin trace consciousness to material and colonial conditions, so character is inferred to be shaped by circumstance.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the movement's appeal to the UN Charter and legal self-determination, though Fanon records single-party leaders ruling above law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; adherents have no shared view on space as a civilizational goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream favours popular sovereignty and mass democracy over a mix with aristocratic elements.

leader-cult.rationale: Fanon warns that the cult of the leader reflects a failing national bourgeoisie, though several anti-colonial states practised it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-law custody is outside anti-imperialism; the left-leaning mainstream has no shared line on it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not stated as such; inferred from Fanon's warning that the native middle class and party leaders can capture the post-colonial state.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's peasant-centred anti-colonial program and the left-leaning Third World mainstream, which broke up colonial and landlord estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial support for the displaced, notably Palestinians; the sources do not address return directly.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Bandung's principles stress respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity of all nations, which cuts against claims on neighbours' land.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the secular, left-leaning mainstream, which treated religious coercion as backward; not addressed in the sources.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the secular, left-leaning mainstream; not addressed in the sources.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's critique of neocolonial dependence; shared currencies such as the CFA franc are read as colonial relics.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from Bandung-era Afro-Asian and pan-African solidarity, which favored unity among kindred peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist tradition of national equality and cultural rights for minorities within a state; not stated in the cited chapter.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist preference for equal rights in the country of residence over separate homelands; not stated in the cited chapter.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Lenin's account of imperialism as monopoly and finance capital is a materialist explanation of historical change.

ban-cartels.rationale: Lenin treats monopoly as an inevitable product of capitalism, so the remedy is socialism, not trust-busting.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from hostility to finance capital; anti-imperialists oppose rescuing banks, though many would support state rescue of national industry.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Adherents are split: popular sovereignty and distrust of bourgeois institutions pull one way, protection of rights and rules the other.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream's support for women's equality; not addressed in the sources.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Anti-imperialists reject colonial blocs, though Fanon-style self-reliance would favor limiting dependence; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from Third World suspicion that rich-country trade conditions work as disguised protectionism.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; moral incentives were a Cuban and Guevarist idea rather than a general anti-imperialist one.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Fanon defends revolutionary violence as the way colonized peoples free themselves; inferred as support for armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the anti-feudal, anti-colonial mainstream, which opposed inherited rank; not stated in the sources.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Fanon urges reclaiming the pre-colonial national past against colonial history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Bandung condemned colonialism in all its manifestations, and the tradition rejects civilizing justifications for rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred: nation-building anti-colonial movements promoted national pride in schools, though Fanon warned of its pitfalls.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream left anti-colonial strand backed remedies for racial injustice.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: Third World states sought national control of finance, though the sources do not address money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Lenin treats imperialism as parasitic, decaying capitalism driving war, not an adapting system.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Opposition to great-power spheres of influence is central; Bandung bars big-power domination.

delink-world-market.rationale: Contested: Fanon urges breaking ties with the former colonizer, but Bandung also called for economic cooperation.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's view that imperial profits bribe a layer of workers in the rich countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: the strand upholds equality of peoples and races and opposes discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred: Bandung endorsed human rights and the UN Charter, though adherents prioritised sovereignty.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-imperialists condemn partitions imposed without consent and Bandung condemned colonialism in all its forms, yet post-colonial states mostly kept the inherited borders (compare keep-colonial-borders), so the lean is modest.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from self-determination: peoples should choose their own rulers, though many anti-colonial states were one-party.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: national liberation movements rely on collective majority decision, not individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial tradition of resisting illegitimate rule, applied to rulers generally.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: anti-colonial movements sought elected national assemblies over colonial governors and monarchs.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from general leftist moral outlook.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream left acceptance of regulated animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: the strand favors solidarity and structural change over paternal duties of the privileged.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: Lenin and Fanon call for organized political action against domination.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's view that colonial culture and the native elite's borrowed culture sustain domination.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's account of the native middle class and cultural dependence helping maintain the system.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Lenin's theory of finance capital and Fanon's neocolonialism both say wealth flows from poor countries to richer ones.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand is civic and internationalist, though Fanon criticizes nativist tribalism.

party-own-road.rationale: Bandung-era non-interference and national self-determination imply each country's party chooses its own path.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's call to break dependence, though non-aligned states also sought cooperation and aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: Bandung stressed respect for territorial integrity and the anti-colonial era generally accepted colonial borders.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from national liberation by colonized natives over settler rule, though settlers' status varies by case.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from the leftist alignment of the mainstream strand.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist anti-imperialists reject equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist and anti-colonial view of slavery as central to American capitalism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: decolonization commonly removed colonial symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from left framing that treats women's disadvantage as structural; not addressed in sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the same left framing; not addressed in sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: anti-imperialists reject imposed Western models and favor each people's own path, though Bandung affirmed human rights.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's warnings about the post-colonial elite; Bandung stresses civilian state sovereignty.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from left calls for social provision and recognition of labor.

filial-duty.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern; inferred from the anti-colonial mainstream's attachment to community and kin solidarity against colonial individualism.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's stress on popular, anti-colonial mass politics over mandarin-style rule by examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign control of national industry is the core complaint: Lenin ties imperialism to foreign finance capital and Bandung stresses economic sovereignty.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-leaning, secular mainstream, which generally favored modern family law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Fanon's demand that leaders answer to the masses rather than a national bourgeoisie.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which expected public social provision rather than private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Fanon's call to return land to the people and anti-colonial land reform against settler ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the anti-colonial demand for self-government through representative institutions.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from post-colonial nation-building, which often promoted a common national language, though many adherents defended local languages against colonial ones.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial aim of ending foreign economic control, including settler and foreign land holdings.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between the left's concern with structural inequality and nationalist wariness of imported frameworks.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist and Third World critique of consumer capitalism and Western affluence built on empire.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The mainstream backed national liberation movements against colonial rule, though Bandung bars interference in others' internal affairs, so support is for anti-colonial struggles.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bandung's principles forbid intervention or interference in the internal affairs of another country; opposing great-power domination of allies is the core of the doctrine.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lenin described finance capital and the banks as fusing with the state and driving imperial policy.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the view that foreign money is an instrument of domination; the sources do not address NGO funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern as such and adherents differ.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from opposition to foreign economic domination, including foreign acquisition of national land.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning anti-colonial mainstream, which expected independent states to provide work.

democratic-peace.rationale: Lenin and later anti-imperialists treat great-power democracy promotion as a cover for domination.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents are split; the tradition cares about who rules, not obedience to law as such.

non-intervention.rationale: The Bandung principles include abstention from intervention or interference in another country's internal affairs.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist and Third World left, which backed organised labour; the sources do not address union form.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred; the movement's anti-colonial mainstream rejected ethnic conspiracy theories as a divide-and-rule tool.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common position.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to secret great-power diplomacy; Lenin's tradition attacked secret treaties.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's call for national economies not tied to the former rulers, though trade itself is not opposed.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Leninist mainstream relied on parties and mass organisations rather than small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Bandung principles stress sovereignty, and anti-imperialists see international courts as tools of great powers.

religious-nation.rationale: The mainstream strand is secular and leans on nation as a political, not religious, community.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The Bandung principles affirm the equality of all nations and condemn big-power domination.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which favours pooling resources for development; not directly addressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist and socialist mainstream, which targets productive, not personal, property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from Bandung-era non-alignment and peaceful coexistence between systems.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from Fanon's call for nationalised trade and cooperatives, favouring public over private provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the secular, Marxist-influenced mainstream; Islamist strands are outside scope.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Lenin treats capitalism's monopoly stage as parasitic and moribund; Fanon sees it as the colonial legacy, so adherents mostly reject the progressive framing.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the socialist and Marxist mainstream, which ties women's emancipation to economic change.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the socialist mainstream, which expects independent states to socialise domestic services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial cultural revival and reclaiming national languages from colonial ones.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to domination and from the anti-colonial stance on indigenous rights.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Fanon proposes cooperatives and rural communal organisation as the route to genuine independence.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the critique of settler colonialism and state-driven settlement of minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Bandung and the non-aligned movement stood for a path between the two blocs, though the Leninist strand dissents.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Self-determination favours the people living on a land now; inferred from that principle, though some adherents back historical claims of colonised peoples.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred that the mainstream left anti-colonial tradition accepts the historical record.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular, left-leaning mainstream, which generally opposes criminalising private conduct, though some Third World states did.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Fanon warns against single-party elites, yet many anti-imperialist states banned opposition as a defence against foreign subversion; adherents are split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the secular left strand, which does not give the state a role in policing religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Lenin's analysis of imperialism is precisely a critique of colonies held for the markets, raw materials and investment outlets of the ruling powers.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The strand scoped here is secular; armed resistance to invasion is endorsed as national, not as a religious duty on all believers.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the secular strand and its stress on national self-government rather than religious legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Fanon calls for the mass of people to take part directly in running the new nation rather than leaving it to a national elite.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Lenin and Fanon link colonial racial hierarchy to capitalist exploitation, so the strand treats them as intertwined; inferred from that.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from the left-leaning strand's general support for recognition of oppressed groups.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between left-liberal support and traditionalist opposition in Third World states.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The strand is firmly on the left and treats imperialism as a product of capital, so it keeps the left-right divide.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Marxist-Leninist roots of the mainstream strand.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from the secular strand, which opposes colonial 'civilising' narratives that cast other cultures as inferior.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The strand rests on popular self-determination, so authority comes from the people rather than from God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from secular republican bans to defence of local religious dress against colonial imposition.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-leaning strand's support for worker protections.

social-market-economy.rationale: The strand holds that formal independence means little while economies stay dependent, favouring state-led development over open markets; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; independent states in the tradition kept armies to defend against intervention.

rich-first.rationale: Fanon and Lenin criticise uneven development under imperialism and call for equitable development of the former colonies.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Bandung-era non-aligned movement was founded on staying out of the Cold War blocs. The sources set out the underlying principle but do not state a position on this specific statement.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from the secular, republican anti-colonial mainstream, which condemned inherited privilege and the native elites that Fanon criticizes.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Fanon favours cooperatives, but the ideology has no stated view on user-owned credit banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from its critique of neocolonial dependence: lender conditions are seen as a way for former rulers to keep control.

property-franchise.rationale: Self-determination and anti-colonial struggle rest on broad popular rule, and wealth-limited franchises recall colonial exclusion.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The tradition did not address the link between domination of women and of nature; adherents are split.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist tradition, which sees capitalist forces as ruling people while hiding that relation.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist view that finance capital and monopoly control the press, though the sources do not discuss it.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from Bandung's endorsement of the UN Charter and human rights, which imply law-bound government.

racial-franchise.rationale: Bandung declared the equality of all races and condemned racial discrimination.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; the mainstream tradition is silent on online participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the human-rights and anti-secrecy stance against great-power dealings; the sources do not address it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Bandung upheld human rights and equality of religions, so state limits on marriage across faiths would be rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Bandung condemned discrimination and promoted solidarity across peoples, so boycotts by owner religion would be rejected.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern as such; inferred from Fanon's call for broad popular political education and participation over elite rule, which sits comfortably with lot-chosen citizen deliberation.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from the secular, modernizing left-leaning mainstream, which wanted inherited religious authority subordinated to reason and national development; the religion question was not central.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist and Third World view that finance capital and monopoly drive domination, so concentrated wealth threatens self-government.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern; the anti-colonial mainstream took no common position on it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Bandung-era mainstream was secular but pluralist and did not make state atheism policy; inferred at low confidence.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Anti-imperial movements saw police and prisons as colonial tools but the post-colonial states they built kept them; inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition stressed national unity against colonial divide-and-rule rather than prescribing power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The left-leaning mainstream expected independent states to provide social services and viewed charity as inadequate; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; one-party and long-serving leaders were common in the movement. Inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: The ideology never addressed vote delegation; inferred neutral.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition focused on imperial war and domination rather than extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist question; adherents are split across secular and religious strands.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the anti-colonial mainstream's egalitarian and modernizing leanings, though it seldom discusses marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not a concern of the anti-imperialist tradition; inferred as split.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist left's hostility to rentier and finance-capital income, which extends to landlords.

abolish-ip.rationale: Third World states pressed for technology transfer, but abolishing patents was not a stated aim; inferred as split.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is not defined by youth drill, and its secular left leans toward voluntary organisation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The Bandung-era movement called for the prohibition of nuclear weapons, so hosting them would be rejected.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign military presence is a form of great-power domination that the movement opposes, and Bandung rejected great-power military pacts.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: the tradition documents colonial atrocities and would favour formal acknowledgement of them.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Lenin attacks the rentier state and the 'coupon-clipping' parasitism of finance capital, which income from ownership alone represents.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Fanon defends the necessity of armed violence against colonial rule, so absolute pacifism is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Fanon values the national past as part of the struggle but warns against its romanticising; adherents are split.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; inferred as split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; inferred as split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's honouring of those who died in liberation struggles.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand is secular and materialist, treating politics as a struggle of classes and powers.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand seeks sovereign states for the peoples living in them, not a diaspora centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: Fanon ties culture to the liberation struggle rather than putting it before state-building.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; inferred as split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; inferred as split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Fanon criticises a national middle class that takes over from colonial rulers and condemns exclusion of minorities.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream strand; inferred as split.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: Fanon warns that a nationalist party can become a tool of a new elite, which supports workers' organizations free of it.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from the Leninist strand, which ties socialism to working-class rule, though some anti-colonial leaders called state-led development socialist.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which wanted essential services under public control after independence.

second-chamber.rationale: The anti-imperialist core is about sovereignty, not legislative structure; no position can be inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: The Leninist and Third World mainstream looked to national ownership of resources, not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is concerned with national self-determination rather than local confederation.

family-wage.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern; no position can be inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern; critiques of drug-company power pull one way and access to treatment the other.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the Third World focus on basic health and development needs ahead of life-extension research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Anti-imperialists dislike sanctions and dollar dominance, which favors payments beyond state reach, but they also back state economic control; split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed by the anti-imperialist core; no position can be inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Fanon values the human person but the mainstream subordinates individuals to national and class liberation; adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The mainstream strand is secular, but anti-colonial movements also drew on religious and cultural revival, so no clear position.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; no position can be inferred from principles of self-determination.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the Third World concern with dependence on foreign agribusiness and seed patents.

dense-cities.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern; no position can be inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Anti-colonial movements organized around racial and colonized-peoples solidarity (Bandung, Fanon), though the mainstream also stresses non-racial class and national unity.

racial-pride.rationale: Fanon and negritude-era anti-colonialism affirmed pride in colonized peoples' identity against colonial denigration, though Fanon warns against racial chauvinism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Bandung principles respect sovereignty and call for refraining from aggression, and allow self-defence; wars of liberation make this less than strong.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The mainstream strand stressed shared struggle and self-determination of colonized peoples; Fanon warned against tribalism, and adherents did not agree on language as the criterion.

communal-electorates.rationale: Fanon criticized tribalism and regionalism after independence, and the anti-colonial mainstream saw colonial communal divisions as a tool of divide and rule.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Anti-imperialists hold that great powers use division and intervention to keep weaker states dependent, and Bandung condemned such intervention.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning anti-colonial mainstream, which expected independent states to provide education to all.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the Third World strand held that rich industrial countries caused pollution and should not burden poorer states, and preferred state-led development over market tools.

future-generations.rationale: The mainstream strand focused on independence and development, and the sources do not show a position on duties to future generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Anti-colonial movements promoted women's participation, but the sources show no claim that women bring distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Bandung and the non-aligned movement called for disarmament and condemned great-power arms races and defense pacts, though newly independent states also armed themselves.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialist denunciation of secret great-power treaties; Lenin published the secret treaties after 1917, though the sources do not state this.

capital-controls.rationale: Fanon and the Bandung-era mainstream saw foreign finance as a route to neocolonial dependence and favored national control over capital and resources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: anti-colonial movements fought through armed liberation groups and the tradition defends resistance forces' right to arms against foreign domination.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Split: Lenin urged turning imperialist wars into revolutionary struggle, but national liberation wars are defended and soldiers' refusal is not a general rule.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which backs unions; labour bargaining is not central to the anti-imperialist core.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern; the left-leaning mainstream favours state welfare but tax credits are a specific rich-country device.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: Third World thought treats externally imposed fiscal discipline as a tool of dependency and favours sovereign economic policy.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Lenin ties imperialism to the division of the world among finance capital, and the Bandung-era movement demanded a fairer international economic order for the colonised.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Split: Leninists favour smashing the state machine, while Bandung-era nationalist governments took over and used the inherited state; Fanon warns of the national bourgeoisie.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream held varied socialist blueprints and nationalisation, yet stressed each people's right to choose its own path.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: pricing nature is seen as extending capitalist commodification, though not discussed in the sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: Fanon criticises nationalist cults and the secular left-leaning mainstream treats the nation as a political, liberating community, not a sacred one.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream's hostility to debt as dependency; student loans are not an anti-imperialist topic.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The tradition extends colonial analysis to the exploitation of regions and peoples inside states, and Fanon describes the national bourgeoisie and capital draining the interior.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: claims of equal dignity underpin the rejection of colonial racial hierarchy, though Fanon speaks of making a new man.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which supported state-funded media and information independence from foreign control.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The secular-leaning mainstream takes no position on religious truth; inferred neutral.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, whose post-colonial states protected peasants and commodity producers from dependence on foreign markets.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Bandung-era non-aligned states urged banning nuclear weapons, but adherents split on whether a state should disarm alone; inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: Lenin's tradition built independent working-class parties; inferred for the mainstream strand, though Fanon distrusted party elites.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anti-imperialists split between condemning the practice and resisting outside intervention on custom; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning anti-colonial mainstream's commitment to equality.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; neutral.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning preference for state rules over private lawsuits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Fanon criticises customary chiefs as collaborators of colonial rule, and the mainstream favoured modern national government; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not an anti-imperialist concern; adherents split and the sources are silent.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; no clear position among adherents.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; neutral.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which backed union strength; the issue is not part of the anti-imperialist core.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-leaning strand, which treats ID rules as a barrier to participation.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the secular, left-leaning anti-colonial mainstream would favor equal standing among religious interpretations, inferred from that.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from Lenin's and Fanon's view that formal elections mean little while economic dependence persists, so procedure alone does not make a state democratic.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular, left-leaning mainstream that accepted social liberalization.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strand's emphasis on popular self-determination and civil liberties against state power.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the left mainstream favored public services, but a cash-transfer replacement is not an anti-imperialist question.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not addressed directly; the anti-colonial mainstream demanded equal political rights for all, inferred from that.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between secular critics of religion and those who see religion as a source of anti-colonial resistance.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the strand's rejection of colonial racial hierarchy.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-leaning mainstream's support for state programs on equality.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Lenin and Fanon regard property claims by settlers and companies as products of conquest, and favour collective or state ownership.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Adherents are split: they back prosecuting aggression but often distrust Western-dominated courts as instruments of great powers; Bandung did not address criminal courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream strand is secular, and the scope excludes Islamist anti-imperialism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: the left anti-colonial mainstream endorsed equality, but gender guarantees in self-government were not a stated demand.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Leninist anti-imperialism backed socialist states against capitalist encirclement and imperialist attack, though it did not always endorse bureaucratic rule.

indirect-election.rationale: Adherents differ: Leninists supported council systems while Fanon criticised one-party rule and favoured popular participation.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the secular, left character of the mainstream strand.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Self-determination of peoples is the core claim, and Leninist doctrine granted national territories autonomy; Fanon criticised tribalism and regionalism.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Bandung and the anti-imperialist tradition stress the right of peoples to self-determination, which supports popular decision on a territory's allegiance.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The Bandung-era states, and the later Organisation of African Unity, upheld inherited boundaries to avoid conflict, while Fanon warned of tribalism that would break states apart.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the mainstream anti-imperialist strand; no position can be inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the tradition opposes settler colonialism, which implies restricting outside settlement of indigenous homelands.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed; anti-colonial states varied on conscription and on women's military service.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Fanon ties national culture and land to the anti-colonial struggle, but a spiritual duty to ancestral land is not a stated Bandung-era doctrine; inferred from its defence of peoples' attachment to their territory.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Anti-colonial movements condemned colonial summary violence and defended due process and human rights; Bandung's declaration upholds fundamental human rights and the UN Charter.

close-ties-china.rationale: Bandung-era non-alignment sought independence from both blocs and welcomed China as a fellow Asian-African state; leaning toward China over the US is inferred from opposition to great-power domination.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Anti-colonialism stressed respect for borders and non-interference, which cuts against kin-state claims, yet backs solidarity with oppressed peoples; adherents are split and the sources do not address it.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Lenin and Fanon see resources as the people's wealth taken by monopolies and call for national or public control; a compensation-to-all principle is inferred, not stated.

self-ownership.rationale: The mainstream leftist strand stresses liberation from domination but also collective claims on labour; the sources do not discuss self-ownership, so this is neutral.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not address tax structure; the left-leaning strand would dislike regressive consumption taxes, but newly independent states relied on them, so adherents are split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Fanon and Third World socialism favour broad public services for the whole people, inferred from its egalitarian, left-leaning lean rather than any stated position on means testing.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Fanon warns of a leader cut off from the masses and urges party and popular organisation, though some Third World leaders ruled through personal appeal; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Fanon attacks the national bourgeoisie for living on privileges and concessions from the former rulers; opposition to favoured business is inferred from this.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The mainstream strand is secular and aimed at unifying a nation across communal lines, as Fanon argues against tribal and ethnic division; the scope notes it is secular-leaning.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Anti-colonial writers wanted modern development and also cultural revival (Fanon on national culture), but the sources set out no combination; split and inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The secular, left-leaning strand backed women's equal rights as part of liberation, though the sources do not discuss divorce law; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Lenin sees foreign capital's control of colonies' resources as the core of imperialism, and Bandung affirmed each nation's sovereignty over its natural resources and wealth.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Lenin and Fanon see existing property and wealth as products of colonial plunder and dependence, so they judge distribution by outcome.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist critique of finance capital, which favours checks on speculative finance; the sources do not name this tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Fanon and the anti-colonial tradition treat racism and its colonial legacy as a central obstacle to the colonized.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial movements that disobeyed colonial law as illegitimate, though the sources do not state a theory of law.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the left-leaning mainstream, which expects technology to serve development; the sources do not address automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Bandung principles reject domination by great powers and big-power blocs, favouring independent states and non-alignment.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Lenin's analysis is in the Marxist tradition, which holds that labour is the source of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Fanon and the Bandung-era movements joined national consciousness with serving the people, and Lenin backed national liberation by the working masses.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: national and racial identity were central to the anti-colonial struggle, so adherents would not put material interests alone first.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Adherents are split, since some post-colonial states took this path and the sources do not settle it.

missingStatements.text: Foreign military bases on another country's soil should be removed.
missingStatements.rationale: Foreign troops and bases are a standard marker of imperial domination, and Bandung's principles bar using defence arrangements to serve big-power interests.

missingStatements.text: Formerly colonized countries should nationalize resources and industries owned by foreign companies.
missingStatements.rationale: Fanon calls for nationalizing trade and breaking economic ties to the former colonizer, which post-colonial states did with foreign-owned assets.

notes: Highly strand-dependent: Islamist and right-wing anti-imperialists would answer religion, family and market questions oppositely; the liberal Hobson strand rejects the claim that capitalism causes imperialism. Bandung was cited via Wikipedia because the communique text was not accessible.
